subject: sociology

moments.title: Schooling in Capitalist America
moments.body: Bowles and Gintis argue US schools reproduce class relations through a 'correspondence' between school discipline and workplace hierarchies.
moments.takeaway: Education's hidden curriculum aligns students with the labour market.

moments.title: Learning to Labour
moments.body: Willis's ethnography of West Midlands 'lads' shows working-class boys actively producing their own class trajectory through counter-school culture.

moments.title: Bowles and Gintis revisit
moments.body: Their Sociology of Education paper revisits the correspondence thesis, qualifying it but defending core claims.
moments.takeaway: Major theses get revisited as labour markets change.

now.title: Schools and inequality
now.body: Sociology of education uses both correspondence-style and Bourdieusian frameworks, alongside policy-focused 'closing the gap' research.
now.open_questions: How does the rise of credential inflation alter the correspondence between schooling and work?

reflection: Bowles and Gintis's book remains in print because the question of what school is for remains open.
